inline_comments.comment: This file is a development scratch/process document and should not be committed to the repository. The same applies to `PR_SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md`, `WARDLEY_MAPS_MEDIUM_GUIDE.md`, and `WARDLEY_MAPS_USER_GUIDE.md`. These contain PR checklists, internal notes, and blog-style content that belong outside version control (or in `demos/dev/` if a draft). Committed root-level artifact files add noise to the repository history and `git log`.

`packages/mermaid/src/config.type.ts` is auto-generated from `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml` and must not be modified manually — the file's own header comment says "DO NOT MODIFY IT BY HAND". The `WardleyDiagramConfig` interface and the `'wardley-beta'` property on `MermaidConfig` were added here directly instead of being generated. Re-run the project's type-generation build script after updating the schema so the types stay in sync and future schema changes don't silently diverge.

The detector regex uses the `/i` case-insensitive flag: `/^\s*wardley-beta/i`. All other diagram detectors in the project (e.g., xychart, treemap, radar) are case-sensitive and do not use `/i`. Using a case-insensitive match is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase and could silently accept `WARDLEY-BETA` or `Wardley-Beta`, which the grammar's `KW_WARDLEY: 'wardley-beta'` terminal would then reject. Remove the `i` flag.

`getConfig()` is called once inside `getTheme()` (line 26) and again inside `getConfigValues()` (line 44). Both helpers are then called at the top of `draw()` (lines 61–62), producing two redundant config reads per render. The established pattern in other renderers (e.g., radar, xychart) is to call `getConfig()` once at the top of `draw`, destructure the relevant sections, and pass values down as explicit parameters. Refactor both helpers to accept a config/themeVariables argument instead of calling `getConfig()` internally.

`themeVariables.wardley` is accessed throughout `getTheme()` but no `wardley` namespace is registered in any of Mermaid's theme files (`theme-base.js`, `theme-default.js`, etc.) — this PR does not touch those files. As a result, the optional chaining `?.` will always evaluate to `undefined` and every property will fall through to the hardcoded defaults. The theme customization API advertised in the documentation is therefore entirely non-functional. Either register the `wardley` theme variables in all five built-in theme files, or remove the theme-override paths and rely solely on the fallback values until proper theme integration is added.

`viewBox` is set via d3's `.attr('viewBox', ...)`. D3 (and some DOM wrappers) may lowercase attribute names, rendering it as `viewbox`, which is silently ignored by SVG engines because the attribute is case-sensitive. Use the native DOM API instead:
```ts
svg.node()?.setAttribute('viewBox', `0 0 ${width} ${height}`);
```
This matches the pattern used in other renderers such as `pieRenderer.ts`.

The new demo page at `demos/wardley.html` is not linked from `demos/index.html`. The project convention requires every new demo file to be registered there so it appears in the demo index. Add a `
  • Wardley Maps
    • ` entry to `demos/index.html`.

`configValues.nodeRadius * 1.6` uses an unexplained magic number. Extract it to a named constant at the top of the file:
```ts
const PIPELINE_SQUARE_TO_RADIUS_RATIO = 1.6;
```
Similar issues exist at line 79 (`1.05` title font size multiplier) and inside the annotations box calculation (`105` pixel buffer). Magic numbers make the rendering arithmetic opaque and difficult to tune.

`styles: () => ''` is included as a placeholder. Other diagram types (treemap, sankey, etc.) point `styles` to a real `getStyles` function from a co-located `styles.ts` module. If no custom SVG styles are needed, the property should be omitted entirely (per the project rule: omit optional properties that are not yet implemented) rather than including a no-op stub. If styles are planned, add a minimal `styles.ts` with a `DiagramStylesProvider`-typed export.

The `LINK_ARROW` terminal includes a bare `'>'` alternative:
```langium
terminal LINK_ARROW: '-->' | '-.->' | '>' | ...;
```
A standalone `>` doesn't correspond to any documented Wardley link syntax and could match unexpectedly (e.g., in HTML entities or angle-bracket content). If this was inherited from another grammar, it should be removed. If it is intentional, add a documentation example showing its usage and a corresponding parser test.

`Anchor` and `Component` rules use `WARDLEY_NUMBER` (which requires a decimal point, e.g., `0.63`) for their coordinates, while `Annotations`, `Annotation`, `Accelerator`, and `Deaccelerator` use `CoordinateValue` (which accepts both `WARDLEY_NUMBER` and `INT`). This is inconsistent: `annotations [1, 0]` is valid (demonstrated in the GPT Tokeniser E2E test), but `anchor Business [1, 0.63]` would fail to parse because `1` is an `INT`, not a `WARDLEY_NUMBER`. Replace `WARDLEY_NUMBER` with `CoordinateValue` in `Anchor` and `Component` coordinate positions to make the grammar consistent and allow integer coordinates everywhere.

The test suite only covers valid happy-path inputs. Per project conventions, parser specs must also include cases for invalid or malformed inputs that are expected to fail (e.g., a component with only one coordinate, an `evolve` targeting a non-existent component, an out-of-range coordinate value like `[1.5, 0.5]`, a pipeline referencing an undefined parent). The PR description mentioned a `'rejects invalid stage boundaries'` test, but it is not present in the spec file. Add negative test cases.

The field names `ast.annotations` and `ast.annotation` (singular vs. plural) are confusing because both are arrays: `ast.annotations` holds zero-or-more `Annotations` box-position declarations, while `ast.annotation` holds zero-or-more individual `Annotation` markers. A reader naturally expects `ast.annotations` to be the collection of individual annotations. Consider renaming in the grammar: `annotationsBox?=Annotations` (optional single item) and `annotations+=Annotation` (the collection), which would make the intent explicit and align with conventional naming.

general_comments.comment: **Type definitions belong in `types.ts`, not `wardleyBuilder.ts`.** The project convention (enforced across all diagram types) requires that all domain type and interface definitions (`WardleyNode`, `WardleyLink`, `WardleyTrend`, `WardleyPipeline`, `WardleyAnnotation`, `WardleyNote`, `WardleyAccelerator`, `WardleyDeaccelerator`, `WardleyAxesConfig`, `WardleyBuildResult`) live in the diagram's `types.ts` file. Currently these are all defined in `wardleyBuilder.ts`, while `wardleyTypes.ts` contains only the DB type alias. Move the domain interfaces to `wardleyTypes.ts` (or a new `wardleyTypes.ts`) and import from there. This keeps `wardleyBuilder.ts` focused on state-management logic and makes the type contracts independently discoverable.

**Module-level mutable builder state does not use `ImperativeState`.** `wardleyDb.ts` declares a module-level `const builder = new WardleyBuilder()` whose internal Maps and arrays are mutated across parse cycles. The project requires functional-export DB modules to use the `ImperativeState` utility (from `packages/mermaid/src/utils/imperativeState.ts`) for all mutable state so that state is correctly re-initialized from `getConfig()` on each parse. Without this, the current implementation technically resets state on `clear()`, but the pattern is inconsistent with how other diagrams manage state and could break if the module is ever shared across concurrent render paths.

**Cypress E2E test coverage is incomplete.** The spec file (`cypress/integration/rendering/wardley.spec.js`) only contains 6 named tests, not the 12 claimed in the PR description. Several features noted as implemented (source strategy markers, areas, inertia markers, dual-label evolution stages, custom stage widths, accelerators/deaccelerators) do not have dedicated `imgSnapshotTest` cases. Each rendering branch needs at least one snapshot test to prevent future visual regressions, as per the project rules for new diagram types.
